name: Software
description: Root of the full software taxonomy tree

categories.name: System software
categories.description: Manages the computer's hardware and provides a platform for other software.

subcategories.name: Operating systems
subcategories.description: Schedules processes, manages memory and files, and gives every other program a machine to run on.

subcategories.name: Device drivers
subcategories.description: Translates between the operating system and one specific piece of hardware.

subcategories.name: Firmware
subcategories.description: Low-level code stored on the device itself, usually the first thing to run when it powers on.

subcategories.name: Utility software
subcategories.description: Small focused tools that maintain, clean, protect, or repair a system.

subcategories.name: Language processors
subcategories.description: Turns source code into something the machine can actually execute.

subcategories.name: Virtualization software
subcategories.description: Runs whole guest operating systems side by side on one physical machine.

subcategories.name: Containerization
subcategories.description: Packages an application with its dependencies so it runs the same anywhere, sharing the host kernel.

subcategories.name: System management
subcategories.description: Watches processes, services, and resources, and starts or stops them.

categories.name: Application software
categories.description: Helps users perform specific tasks or solve problems.

subcategories.name: Productivity
subcategories.description: Documents, spreadsheets, and presentations for everyday knowledge work.

subcategories.name: Creative software
subcategories.description: Tools for making and editing images, video, and audio.

subcategories.name: Communication
subcategories.description: Carries calls, meetings, and messages between people.

subcategories.name: Web browsers
subcategories.description: Fetches and renders web pages, and hosts most modern software.

subcategories.name: Business software
subcategories.description: Runs day-to-day commercial work like sales, invoicing, and accounts.

subcategories.name: Educational
subcategories.description: Teaches, drills, and tracks learning progress.

subcategories.name: Entertainment
subcategories.description: Delivers films, music, and games to an audience.

subcategories.name: Personal finance
subcategories.description: Tracks budgets, spending, and savings for one person or household.

categories.name: Enterprise & business systems
categories.description: Runs an organization's core operations: money, people, customers, and supply.

subcategories.name: ERP
subcategories.description: One system of record for finance, inventory, and operations across a whole company.

subcategories.name: CRM
subcategories.description: Tracks customers, deals, and every interaction a company has with them.

subcategories.name: Human resources (HCM)
subcategories.description: Manages hiring, payroll, benefits, and employee records.

subcategories.name: Supply chain & procurement
subcategories.description: Plans inventory, sources suppliers, and moves goods.

subcategories.name: IT service management
subcategories.description: Routes tickets, incidents, and change requests through an IT team.

subcategories.name: Enterprise content management
subcategories.description: Stores, versions, and governs a company's documents.

categories.name: Design & prototyping
categories.description: Plans how software looks and behaves before it gets built.

subcategories.name: Interface design
subcategories.description: Draws screens, components, and layouts before any code exists.

subcategories.name: Prototyping
subcategories.description: Makes a design clickable so the interaction can be tested.

subcategories.name: Whiteboarding & diagramming
subcategories.description: Open canvases for sketching flows and thinking together.

subcategories.name: Design systems & handoff
subcategories.description: Publishes reusable components and specs for engineers to build from.

subcategories.name: 3D & motion
subcategories.description: Models, animates, and renders moving or three-dimensional assets.

categories.name: Programming software
categories.description: Used to create, test, and maintain other software.

subcategories.name: Integrated dev environments
subcategories.description: An editor, a debugger, and a build system in one application.

subcategories.name: Code editors
subcategories.description: Lighter text editors focused on fast, plain code editing.

subcategories.name: Version control
subcategories.description: Records every change and lets people work on the same code at once.

subcategories.name: Build & automation
subcategories.description: Compiles, bundles, and runs repeatable jobs on demand.

subcategories.name: Package managers
subcategories.description: Installs libraries and resolves the versions they depend on.

subcategories.name: Frameworks & libraries
subcategories.description: Pre-built structure and code you build an application on top of.

subcategories.name: Editor extensions
subcategories.description: Adds linting, formatting, or tooling to an editor you already use.

subcategories.name: Testing frameworks
subcategories.description: Structures and runs automated checks against your code.

subcategories.name: Debuggers
subcategories.description: Pauses a running program so you can inspect its state.

subcategories.name: Other dev tools
subcategories.description: Everything else on the workbench, from API clients to infrastructure tooling.

categories.name: Testing & quality assurance
categories.description: Verifies that software behaves correctly, performs well, and stays usable.

subcategories.name: Unit testing
subcategories.description: Checks one function or class in isolation, fast and in bulk.

subcategories.name: End-to-end testing
subcategories.description: Drives the real interface the way a user would, top to bottom.

subcategories.name: API testing
subcategories.description: Sends requests to an endpoint and asserts on what comes back.

subcategories.name: Performance & load
subcategories.description: Puts a system under simulated traffic to find where it slows or breaks.

subcategories.name: Static analysis
subcategories.description: Finds defects by reading the source, without ever running it.

subcategories.name: Accessibility testing
subcategories.description: Checks that software works with screen readers, keyboards, and contrast rules.

subcategories.name: Test management
subcategories.description: Organizes test cases, runs, and results across a team.

categories.name: Middleware
categories.description: Acts as a bridge between applications, systems, or services.

subcategories.name: Application servers
subcategories.description: Hosts server-side applications and manages their requests and lifecycles.

subcategories.name: Message brokers
subcategories.description: Passes messages between services so neither has to wait on the other.

subcategories.name: API gateways
subcategories.description: One front door that routes, authenticates, and rate-limits API traffic.

subcategories.name: Integration platforms
subcategories.description: Connects separate business systems and keeps their data in step.

subcategories.name: Database middleware
subcategories.description: A common interface between application code and whichever database sits behind it.

subcategories.name: Auth & identity
subcategories.description: Proves who a user is and issues the tokens other services trust.

categories.name: Database software
categories.description: Stores, manages, and retrieves data.

subcategories.name: Relational (SQL)
subcategories.description: Tables with fixed schemas and joins between them, queried in SQL.

subcategories.name: NoSQL
subcategories.description: Flexible document, column, or key-value stores that trade joins for scale.

subcategories.name: In-memory
subcategories.description: Keeps data in RAM for microsecond reads, usually as a cache.

subcategories.name: Time-series
subcategories.description: Optimized for measurements written in time order and queried by range.

subcategories.name: Graph databases
subcategories.description: Stores relationships as first-class data and traverses them quickly.

subcategories.name: Data warehouses
subcategories.description: Holds large historical datasets for analytics rather than transactions.

subcategories.name: Distributed
subcategories.description: Spreads one logical database across many machines or regions.

categories.name: Web software
categories.description: Runs in a web browser and is accessed over the internet (or intranet).

subcategories.name: Web applications
subcategories.description: Full software delivered through a browser, with nothing to install.

subcategories.name: Progressive web apps
subcategories.description: Web apps that install, work offline, and behave like native ones.

subcategories.name: Single page applications
subcategories.description: Loads once, then rewrites the page in place as you navigate.

subcategories.name: Multi-page applications
subcategories.description: Requests a fresh page from the server on every navigation.

subcategories.name: Static site generators
subcategories.description: Builds plain HTML ahead of time, so nothing has to run at request time.

subcategories.name: Web frameworks
subcategories.description: Provides routing, templating, and data access for server-side web code.

subcategories.name: Web servers
subcategories.description: Accepts HTTP requests and returns files or hands them to an application.

categories.name: E-commerce & payments
categories.description: Sells goods and services online and moves money between buyers and sellers.

subcategories.name: Commerce platforms
subcategories.description: A whole storefront: catalog, cart, checkout, and admin.

subcategories.name: Headless commerce
subcategories.description: Commerce as an API, leaving the storefront for you to build.

subcategories.name: Payment processing
subcategories.description: Moves money from a buyer's card or account to the merchant.

subcategories.name: Point of sale
subcategories.description: Takes payment and tracks stock at a physical counter.

subcategories.name: Billing & subscriptions
subcategories.description: Charges recurring plans and handles upgrades, proration, and failed payments.

subcategories.name: Marketplaces
subcategories.description: Sells through someone else's storefront alongside other sellers.

categories.name: No-code / low-code platforms
categories.description: Lets people build apps and automate workflows with minimal hand-written code.

subcategories.name: App builders
subcategories.description: Assembles working applications from visual components instead of code.

subcategories.name: Website builders
subcategories.description: Designs and publishes sites by arranging blocks on a page.

subcategories.name: Automation / workflow
subcategories.description: Connects apps so an event in one triggers an action in another.

subcategories.name: Database & backend builders
subcategories.description: Spreadsheet-like data stores that hand you an API for free.

categories.name: Cloud software
categories.description: Runs on remote servers and is accessed over the internet (cloud).

subcategories.name: Infrastructure as a service
subcategories.description: Rented virtual machines, disks, and networks that you configure yourself.

subcategories.name: Platform as a service
subcategories.description: You deploy the code, the provider runs the servers under it.

subcategories.name: Software as a service
subcategories.description: Finished software you subscribe to rather than install.

subcategories.name: Serverless computing
subcategories.description: Runs a function on demand and bills only while it executes.

subcategories.name: Cloud storage
subcategories.description: Durable object storage reachable over the network.

subcategories.name: CDN
subcategories.description: Caches content close to users so it arrives faster.

subcategories.name: Cloud native tools
subcategories.description: Built for elastic, containerized systems rather than fixed servers.

categories.name: Networking & communication
categories.description: Manages, monitors, and enables communication across networks and devices.

subcategories.name: Network operating systems
subcategories.description: The software running inside routers and switches.

subcategories.name: Network management & monitoring
subcategories.description: Watches traffic and device health, and captures packets when something is wrong.

subcategories.name: Software-defined networking
subcategories.description: Controls the network from software instead of device-by-device configuration.

subcategories.name: VoIP & messaging
subcategories.description: Carries voice, SMS, and real-time messages over IP.

subcategories.name: Protocols & libraries
subcategories.description: The agreed formats machines talk in, and the code that speaks them.

categories.name: Media & streaming
categories.description: Encodes, processes, and delivers audio and video content.

subcategories.name: Encoding & processing
subcategories.description: Converts, compresses, and transforms audio and video files.

subcategories.name: Streaming servers
subcategories.description: Ingests a live feed and serves it out to viewers.

subcategories.name: Streaming platforms
subcategories.description: Consumer services that host and distribute the stream.

subcategories.name: DRM & protection
subcategories.description: Encrypts content and controls who is allowed to play it.

categories.name: DevOps & infrastructure
categories.description: Automates building, deploying, and operating software reliably at scale.

subcategories.name: CI/CD pipelines
subcategories.description: Builds, tests, and ships every change automatically.

subcategories.name: Infrastructure as code
subcategories.description: Declares servers and services in files that can be reviewed and replayed.

subcategories.name: Configuration management
subcategories.description: Brings machines to a described state and keeps them there.

subcategories.name: Container orchestration
subcategories.description: Schedules containers across a cluster and restarts whatever dies.

subcategories.name: Monitoring & observability
subcategories.description: Collects metrics and traces so you can see what a system is doing.

subcategories.name: Logging
subcategories.description: Gathers, indexes, and searches log output from everywhere at once.

subcategories.name: Secrets management
subcategories.description: Stores credentials and keys, and hands them out under policy.

categories.name: Security software
categories.description: Protects systems, networks, and data from threats and breaches.

subcategories.name: Endpoint security
subcategories.description: Protects individual laptops, phones, and servers from malware and intrusion.

subcategories.name: Network security
subcategories.description: Filters, inspects, and encrypts traffic crossing a network boundary.

subcategories.name: Identity & access management
subcategories.description: Decides who may sign in and what they are allowed to reach.

subcategories.name: Vulnerability scanning
subcategories.description: Probes systems for known weaknesses before an attacker finds them.

subcategories.name: SIEM
subcategories.description: Correlates security events from across the estate into alerts worth acting on.

subcategories.name: Encryption tools
subcategories.description: Makes data unreadable to anyone without the key.

subcategories.name: Penetration testing
subcategories.description: Attacks a system with permission, to prove what a real intruder could do.

categories.name: Malicious software
categories.description: Written to damage, disrupt, or gain unauthorized access. Listed so you can recognize it; the countermeasures sit under Security software.

subcategories.name: Viruses & worms
subcategories.description: Self-replicating code that spreads from file to file or host to host.

subcategories.name: Ransomware
subcategories.description: Encrypts a victim's files and demands payment for the key.

subcategories.name: Spyware & keyloggers
subcategories.description: Watches activity and sends it to someone else without consent.

subcategories.name: Trojans & backdoors
subcategories.description: Poses as something useful while opening access for an attacker.

subcategories.name: Adware & unwanted programs
subcategories.description: Injects advertising or rides along with other installers.

subcategories.name: Botnets
subcategories.description: Networks of compromised machines driven by a remote operator.

categories.name: Data & AI software
categories.description: Processes data and builds, trains, or serves machine learning and AI models.

subcategories.name: Machine learning frameworks
subcategories.description: Defines, trains, and runs models.

subcategories.name: LLM & GenAI tooling
subcategories.description: Builds on large language models and the services around them.

subcategories.name: Data engineering / ETL
subcategories.description: Moves and reshapes data between systems on a schedule.

subcategories.name: Big data processing
subcategories.description: Computes over datasets far too large for one machine.

subcategories.name: Data visualization
subcategories.description: Turns query results into charts and dashboards people can read.

subcategories.name: MLOps
subcategories.description: Versions, deploys, and monitors models once they are in production.

subcategories.name: Notebooks & experimentation
subcategories.description: Interactive code and results side by side, for exploring data.

categories.name: Quantum computing
categories.description: Programs and simulates quantum hardware for problems classical machines handle badly.

subcategories.name: Quantum SDKs
subcategories.description: Builds and runs quantum circuits from a familiar classical language.

subcategories.name: Quantum languages
subcategories.description: Languages written specifically to express quantum programs.

subcategories.name: Simulators
subcategories.description: Runs quantum circuits on classical hardware, so you can test without a real machine.

subcategories.name: Cloud quantum access
subcategories.description: Queues jobs onto real quantum processors over the network.

categories.name: Desktop software
categories.description: Installed and runs natively on a desktop OS (Windows, macOS, Linux).

subcategories.name: Cross-platform desktop
subcategories.description: One codebase that ships to Windows, macOS, and Linux.

subcategories.name: Native Windows
subcategories.description: Built directly on Windows' own UI frameworks.

subcategories.name: Native macOS
subcategories.description: Built directly on Apple's own UI frameworks.

subcategories.name: Native Linux
subcategories.description: Built on the desktop toolkits Linux environments are made of.

subcategories.name: Examples in the wild
subcategories.description: Familiar desktop apps, and the frameworks they were built with.

categories.name: Mobile software
categories.description: Built for phones, tablets, and wearables, where touch and battery life set the rules.

subcategories.name: Native Android
subcategories.description: Built with Android's own language and toolchain.

subcategories.name: Native iOS
subcategories.description: Built with Apple's own language and toolchain.

subcategories.name: Cross-platform
subcategories.description: One codebase that ships to both iOS and Android.

subcategories.name: Mobile backends
subcategories.description: Hosted auth, data, and push, so an app needs no server of its own.

subcategories.name: Distribution & release
subcategories.description: Submits builds to the app stores and gets them to testers.

subcategories.name: Mobile testing
subcategories.description: Drives a real or simulated device to check the app behaves.

categories.name: Game development
categories.description: Builds and runs interactive games across platforms.

subcategories.name: Game engines
subcategories.description: Rendering, physics, audio, and tooling in one environment.

subcategories.name: Physics engines
subcategories.description: Simulates collisions, forces, and rigid bodies.

subcategories.name: Graphics / rendering
subcategories.description: The APIs that put triangles on the GPU.

subcategories.name: Game servers & multiplayer
subcategories.description: Keeps many players in sync inside one shared world.

subcategories.name: Distribution
subcategories.description: The stores that sell and deliver the finished game.

categories.name: AR, VR & spatial computing
categories.description: Places digital content in physical space through headsets, glasses, and phone cameras.

subcategories.name: AR frameworks
subcategories.description: Tracks the camera against the real world so content can sit in it.

subcategories.name: VR platforms
subcategories.description: The SDKs behind headsets and their controllers.

subcategories.name: Spatial operating systems
subcategories.description: Operating systems written for headsets rather than screens.

subcategories.name: Cross-platform XR
subcategories.description: One API across many headsets and browsers.

subcategories.name: 3D capture & content
subcategories.description: Scans, models, and prepares the assets an XR scene is made of.

categories.name: Blockchain & Web3
categories.description: Builds decentralized applications and smart contracts on distributed ledgers.

subcategories.name: Blockchain platforms
subcategories.description: The ledgers that smart contracts and tokens run on.

subcategories.name: Smart contract tools
subcategories.description: Writes, tests, and deploys code that runs on-chain.

subcategories.name: Wallets
subcategories.description: Holds keys and signs transactions on a user's behalf.

subcategories.name: Decentralized apps
subcategories.description: Applications whose backend logic lives on a blockchain.

categories.name: Robotics & automation
categories.description: Programs and controls robots, automated machinery, and industrial hardware.

subcategories.name: Robotics frameworks
subcategories.description: Message passing, drivers, and motion planning for robots.

subcategories.name: Simulation
subcategories.description: Tests robot behaviour in a virtual world before touching hardware.

subcategories.name: Industrial automation
subcategories.description: Programs the controllers that run factory machinery.

subcategories.name: Robotic process automation
subcategories.description: Software robots that click through business applications the way a person would.

categories.name: Embedded & specialized
categories.description: Built for specific devices, systems, or industries.

subcategories.name: Embedded systems
subcategories.description: Software fixed inside a device and built for its exact hardware.

subcategories.name: Real-time software
subcategories.description: Guarantees a response within a deadline, every time.

subcategories.name: Industrial control
subcategories.description: Supervises and operates plant machinery and processes.

subcategories.name: Mobile apps
subcategories.description: Applications installed onto phones, tablets, and wearables.

subcategories.name: Scientific & engineering
subcategories.description: Modelling, simulation, and design for technical work.

subcategories.name: Healthcare software
subcategories.description: Clinical records, imaging, and the systems hospitals run on.

categories.name: Accessibility & assistive tech
categories.description: Makes software usable for people with disabilities.

subcategories.name: Screen readers
subcategories.description: Speaks the interface aloud for blind and low-vision users.

subcategories.name: Magnification & display
subcategories.description: Enlarges or re-colours the screen for low vision.

subcategories.name: Speech & alternative input
subcategories.description: Drives a computer by voice or switch instead of keyboard and mouse.

subcategories.name: Captioning & transcription
subcategories.description: Turns speech into text, live or after the fact.

subcategories.name: Standards & guidelines
subcategories.description: The rules that define what accessible software actually has to do.

categories.name: Licensing & distribution models
categories.description: How software is licensed, priced, and delivered. This branch cuts across every other one above.

subcategories.name: Open source
subcategories.description: Source is public, and the licence sets out what you may do with it.

subcategories.name: Proprietary
subcategories.description: Source stays closed and use is governed by a purchased licence.

subcategories.name: Freemium & shareware
subcategories.description: Free to start, paid to unlock the rest.

subcategories.name: Subscription & usage-based
subcategories.description: Billed per period or per unit consumed, rather than bought outright.

subcategories.name: Public domain & permissive
subcategories.description: Few or no conditions on reuse, including inside closed products.
